preamble: Devoicing of the bilabial implosive to [p]. In the Pearic languages Chong and Pear, Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓ appears as p (*ɓic 'to lie down, sleep' > Chong pìc, Pear pic), where Bru keeps b (bếq). Headley (1985) reconstructs Proto-Pearic *buːl 'drunk' with *b, and the step Proto-Pearic *b > p is filed under b > p. In Katuic, the Chatong dialect of Ngeq has p with a breathy vowel where Bru, Ta'Oi and Katu keep b: Proto-Katuic *ɓic 'lie down, sleep' > pi̤c, *ɓool 'drunk' > po̤ol (Sidwell 2005). Chatong devoices the plain voiced stops in the same way (*dal 'prop up' > ta̤l, *kduŋ 'bag' > katṳŋ), and it keeps b in baar 'two' < *ɓaar and kabom 'hold in the mouth' < *kɓoom. In Southern Kam (Kam-Sui), Wiktionary derives benl /pən⁵⁵/ 'sky' from Proto-Kam-Sui *ɓun¹, where Sui qbenl keeps the preglottalized stop, but the ABVD Southern Dong list records mən55 'sky'. Khmer reached p in two attested steps: Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓaːr 'two' > Old Khmer ពិរ៑ bir > Modern Khmer ពីរ /piː/. These are filed under ɓ > b and b > p. Modern Khmer ɓ and ɗ are secondary, from earlier *p and *t (បី 'three' < Old Khmer ⟨pi⟩ [ɓiː] < *peːʔ; ដៃ 'hand' < *t₁iiʔ), so the two series swapped places.
phoneticEffects: Devoicing, Loss of Implosion, Airstream Change

examples.note: Ngeq (Kriang) keeps b (bool). Chatong keeps b in baar 'two' < *ɓaar and kabom 'hold in the mouth' < *kɓoom.

Sui qbenl keeps the preglottalized stop /ʔb/. Compare Proto-Tai *ɓɯnᴬ (Thai บน). The ABVD Southern Dong list (Long Yaohong & Zheng Guoqiao) gives 'sky' as mən55, so benl with p rests on Wiktionary alone. The sources consulted give only this one example.
